routine: C0/91AC-93E0 — acceleration / auto-target velocity integrator + subpixel->integer-pixel converter (the "$91AC step" in the C0/881E call order). 8-bit A (m=1), 8-bit X (x=1 after SEP), DP=$1D00.
summary: This routine is the per-frame velocity integrator that sits between the edge-clamp (C0/99DE, which leaves the frame's raw per-axis impulse in $1D2E/$1D30) and the position-integration/collision tree (C0/93E1). FIRST (91AC-91F6) it runs an optional AUTO-TARGET hold: when an auto-walk target is active ($00!=0) it forces a constant +-$10 impulse into $2E/$30 to drive the actor toward target coords ($02 vs $0A x, $03 vs $0E y), arriving (==) is recorded in a bit-field $01 and when both axes arrive ($01==3) it advances the target state ($00=2, clear $01). SECOND (91F8-9236) if a "knockback/forced-vector" mode is active ($01BC!=0) it decodes 2 sign+magnitude impulse bytes from control word $0400 into $4E (x) / $4F (y). THIRD (9238-92C8) it INTEGRATES: it adds the frame impulse ($2E/$30), the standing acceleration bias ($24..$29) and the forced impulse ($4E/$4F) into six 8.4 fixed-point subpixel accumulators $3B/$3C and $3D/$3E and $3F/$40 (three position channels x/y each; channels 2 and 3 are gated by $36 bits 1 and 2 and otherwise just track the same $2E/$30). FOURTH (92CA-93CA) it converts each of the six signed 8.4 accumulators into a NON-NEGATIVE integer-pixel-velocity pair (high nibble, arithmetic >>4 of |value|) split by sign into a +slot and a -slot, and rewrites the accumulator to ONLY its sign-extended fractional remainder (the low nibble) so subpixels carry to next frame. $42/$41 = X +/- integer pixels-this-frame; $44/$43 = Y +/- ; $46/$45,$48/$47,$4A/$49,$4C/$4B = the same for the two extra channels. These integer counts are consumed by C0/93E1's per-pixel stepping tree (verified: C0/944B uses $42 as a +X step-loop count, C0/947D uses $41 as -X). LASTLY (93CC-93E0) a countdown timer $4D, when it expires, zeroes the acceleration-bias bytes $24..$29.
dp: $1D00 (set by LDA #$1D00/TCD at C0/9DE1; X becomes 8-bit via SEP #$10 in the d-pad path but this routine does not use X). All "$XX" operands are WRAM $7E:1DXX. Absolute $0400/$01BC are literal $7E:0400/$7E:01BC.
wramReads: $1D00 ($00): auto-target state machine selector; 0=idle (skip block 1), nonzero=seeking. Set to $02 on arrival.
$1D01 ($01): auto-target 'arrived' bitfield. bit0=x reached, bit1=y reached. ==3 -> advance.
$1D02 ($02): current/source X coordinate (low byte) compared (unsigned) against target $0A.
$1D03 ($03): current/source Y coordinate (low byte) compared against target $0E.
$1D0A ($0A): target X (auto-target) AND x speed-scalar gate for the forced impulse ($4E). 0 -> kill $4E.
$1D0E ($0E): target Y AND y speed-scalar gate for the forced impulse ($4F). 0 -> kill $4F.
$1D87 ($87): X subpixel phase byte (low nibble tested for 'settled' at target).
$1D89 ($89): Y subpixel phase byte (low nibble tested).
$1D2E ($2E): frame X impulse from the d-pad/edge-clamp path (seeded from momentum $2A via 88E5, modified by 99DE). Primary X velocity input; added to $3B and the ungated channels.
$1D30 ($30): frame Y impulse (from $2B). Primary Y velocity input; added to $3C and ungated channels.
$1D24..$1D29 ($24-$29): per-channel standing ACCELERATION BIAS bytes (x/y for the 3 channels). Added every frame; auto-cleared when $4D times out.
$1D36 ($36): channel-mode flags. bit1 -> channel2 uses stored vector $37/$38; bit2 -> channel3 uses $39/$3A. Otherwise channels mirror $2E/$30.
$1D37/$1D38 ($37/$38): stored X/Y vector for channel 2 (used when $36 bit1 set; also added in the mirror path).
$1D39/$1D3A ($39/$3A): stored X/Y vector for channel 3 (used when $36 bit2 set; also added in mirror path).
$1D3B..$1D40 ($3B-$40): the six 8.4 signed subpixel ACCUMULATORS (read-modify-write). $3B/$3C = channel1 x/y; $3D/$3E = ch2; $3F/$40 = ch3. These ARE the momentum/inertia store carried across frames.
$1D4E/$1D4F ($4E/$4F): forced-vector impulse x/y (computed in block 2 from $0400, or stale if $01BC==0). Added into accumulators.
$0400 (abs): control word for forced-vector mode. bit0=sign(neg), bit2=x magnitude select, bit1=y magnitude select.
$01BC (abs): forced-vector / knockback mode active flag. 0 -> skip block 2.
wramWrites: $1D2E ($2E): overwritten with +-$10 auto-target impulse in block 1 (only when $00!=0).
$1D00 ($00): set to $02 when both auto-target axes arrive.
$1D01 ($01): bits set via TSB on arrival; cleared to 0 when ==3.

$1D3B..$1D40 ($3B-$40): the six accumulators are rewritten TWICE -- first with the integrated sum (block 3), then with the sign-extended fractional remainder (block 4). Final stored value is the leftover subpixels (-8..+7 in 4-bit), the carried momentum.
$1D41/$1D42 ($41/$42): X integer pixel velocity, NEG/POS. $42=+pixels-this-frame (loop count into 944B), $41=-pixels (into 947D). Exactly one is nonzero.
$1D43/$1D44 ($43/$44): Y integer pixel velocity, NEG/POS (consumed by the Y branches of 93E1's tree).
uncertainties: BLOCK 2 STALENESS: when $01BC==0 the routine does NOT clear $4E/$4F, yet block 3 always ADDs them. In the captured field-walk trace (lines 510-512) $01BC==0 so this path is skipped and $4E/$4F are presumably already 0 from elsewhere. For byte-exactness the C port must reproduce whatever clears $4E/$4F (likely the per-frame state reset or block 2 of a prior frame). Verifier: confirm $4E/$4F are zeroed each frame before this routine when not in forced mode, or treat them as persistent.

BLOCK 1 SIGN CONVENTION: at 91B6 BCC ($02<$0A) the code writes $F0 (-1px) and at 91B8 ($02>$0A) writes $10 (+1px). That is the opposite of a naive 'move toward larger coord = +'. This implies $02/$0A are stored in a convention where the impulse sign is inverted (or $02 is a position and $0A a target measured oppositely). I matched the disassembly literally; verifier should confirm the coordinate polarity against a live auto-walk trace (the captured trace has $00==0 so block 1 never executes).

$1D87/$1D89 DUAL USE: $87 is also INC'd as a step phase inside C0/9452 (the 93E1 tree). Here it is only READ (low nibble) as a 'settled at target' check. Confirm $87/$89 are the same variable and not aliased differently in auto-target vs normal mode.

ARITHMETIC vs LOGICAL SHIFT: block 4 negates first (EOR FF/INC) THEN does 4x LSR on the magnitude, so the >>4 is a LOGICAL shift of a non-negative magnitude -- equivalent to truncation-toward-zero of acc/16. The remainder is the 4 low bits sign-extended. I am confident, but flag because a naive 'arithmetic >>4 of the signed byte' would differ for negatives (it would floor, not truncate).

$36 bit MEANING: I label bit1->channel2, bit2->channel3 'use stored vector $37-$3A'. The exact gameplay meaning (e.g. a fixed scripted move vector vs. live input) is inferred from structure; channels 2/3 themselves feed $45-$4C which the 93E1 tree consumes for what is likely a multi-hitbox / shadow / secondary-actor step. Verifier: identify what $45-$4C actually move (the trace shows them all computed but their consumers past 944B/947D were not fully traced here).

$0A/$0E OVERLOAD: in block 1 these are auto-target coords; in block 2 they gate $4E/$4F as speed scalars. Same addresses, two roles in one routine -- assumed deliberate (auto-target and forced-vector are mutually exclusive in practice). Confirm they are never simultaneously meaningful.
entryPoints: C0/91AC: sole entry, JSR'd from C0/8855 (the player-controller body after 99DE edge-clamp). Falls through to RTS at 93E0; caller then enters the 93E1 step/collision tree.
C0/9238: not a separate entry, but the trace shows this as the join point taken when both block 1 ($00==0) and block 2 ($01BC==0) are skipped -- i.e. the normal field-walk fast path.
callsOut: (none) — C0/91AC-93E0 is straight-line/branch-only with no JSR/JSL/BRL leaving the cluster; it ends in RTS at 93E0. The consumers of its outputs ($41-$4C) are reached only after return, via C0/93E1's JSRs to 944B/947D/94DF/94AD/950F/9545/95AF/9579/95E3/9619/9683.
romTables: (none) — this routine uses no ROM tables. The +-$10 magnitudes, the $0400 bit masks, and the >>4 shift are all immediates. The slope/shape ROM tables (C0/9BF5, 9C0B, 9C21) belong to the 9ADB collision-shape decoder, not here.
